provenance.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Revise ONLY the head/bill and throat silhouette of this Carrion Crow portrait to improve species fidelity. ONE landscape 4:3 finished image.
The current image has a too-deep arched bill and long hanging throat hackles that together suggest a Raven. Correct these two things:
1. Reduce the bill's vertical depth and upper-culmen arch modestly (roughly 15–20 percent), giving it a straighter, less domed top line and modest tip. Retain a stout black CARRION CROW bill, not a thin Rook bill or tiny songbird bill. Keep natural short black feathering over the bill base, no bare pale skin.
2. Shorten the conspicuous long pointed throat feathers into compact close feather texture. The lower throat contour should be smoother, with small drawn feather tips rather than a hanging shaggy beard. Retain rich pencil detail without long Raven hackles.
KEEP EVERYTHING ELSE: the strong original style, black/ink-blue body, precise grouped wing detail, rounded/fan tail shape, feet, pose, dark brown iris, rust angular background, ivory cold-pressed paper, composition, proportions, simple ink ground and exact handwritten text "Carrion Crow". Do not change the background or wing patterns. No extra text, icon, scenery, watermark or props.
The result must still have the same sophisticated slightly stylised print/pigment/coloured-pencil finish, with a clearly Carrion Crow head.

user_review.interpretation: Accepted the preceding review group and authorised continuation to batches 4 and 5.

revision_history.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE finished landscape 4:3 bird portrait for the Birdsong-to-Art collection, filling the image as beautifully as these approved references. Never a grid, contact sheet or storyboard.
REFERENCE ROLES: image 1 is the primary original family style; image 2 supplies expressive contours and printed colour; image 3 supplies sophisticated close-up feather detail; image 4 calibrates clearer graphic feather groups and selective edge contrast. Use these for ARTISTIC LANGUAGE ONLY. Draw the new species' own anatomy and identifying marks.
MEDIUM AND FINISH: warm ivory cold-pressed paper, translucent watercolour underpainting, rich print/gouache-like pigment, broken dry-print grain, economical expressive ink contours, sharp directional coloured-pencil drawing. The bird must read as designed shapes as well as fine texture: clear pigment masses, rhythmic overlapping feather groups, selective dark separations and pale feather edges. Precise detailing lives within larger readable shapes; quiet body passages contrast with intricate focal work. Keep the finish rich and detailed like the originals. No uniform microtexture, photographic airbrushed shading, blanket heavy outline, flat vector simplification or glossy mascot eyes.
CHARACTER: modest expressive stylisation through posture, contour, balance and drawing rhythm while preserving species anatomy. A little surprise in the authored drawing is welcome. No human eyebrows, grin, props, costume, joke, fact caption or repeated literal leaf badge. Do not copy the reference birds' body proportions, yellow beaks, pink legs or eye colours.
COMPOSITION: single dominant whole bird, comfortably inside the landscape frame including full bill, toes and tail. Species-led plumage colours, exposed paper, spare ink support. Simple abstract background shapes only; their precise outline, crop and placement can be invented within the direction below. Material texture compatible with the bird, subordinate to it; no detailed habitat, foliage, building, scenic landscape or ornate frame.
LETTERING: only the exact name supplied below, understated legible dark handwritten lettering beneath the bird. Lower-right corner empty: no sensor state, icon, number or invented encounter data. No signature/watermark or extra text.
SUBJECT: Carrion Crow (Corvus corone), Adult, sex unspecified.
VERIFIED IDENTIFIERS TO PRESERVE:
- Large heavy all-black corvid with glossy plumage
- Stout blunt black bill
- Feathered black face at bill base
- Rounded or fan-shaped tail when spread
Avoid identity confusion: Rook's pale bare face and slender pointed bill; Jackdaw's grey nape and pale iris; Raven's oversized heavy bill and pronounced diamond-shaped tail; Hooded Crow grey body.
ARTISTIC POSE: Grounded broad-bodied left-facing stance with a mild forward lean, strong black bill and black feathered face, measured weight over the feet.
SPECIFIC DRAWING EMPHASIS: Entire bird remains convincingly black: plumage can resolve in near-black, ink-blue and very subtle petrol planes. Selective graphite-grey pencil shafts articulate the wings. No white patches, no grey nape, no pale iris and no Rook's bare bill base. Keep the bill sturdy but not a monstrous Raven bill.
BACKGROUND DIRECTION: One broad incomplete warm rust angular gesture offset behind the body; broken painted edge and generous ivory paper.
PLUMAGE PALETTE: black, ink-blue, graphite. Keep the biology legible; colour accents are in mark-making, not replacements for identifying markings.
TEXT VERBATIM: "Carrion Crow".
revision_history.review: Superseded: deep arched bill and long throat feathers leaned toward Raven.
Selected: slimmer less-arched bill and compact throat texture improve Carrion Crow identity.
